newsitem.title: SURINAM: Suriname says Bouterse case is Dutch political ploy.
newsitem.headline: Suriname says Bouterse case is Dutch political ploy.

text.p: Surinam on Tuesday denounced Dutch plans to arrest former military leader Desi Bouterse for alleged drug smuggling as political manoeuvring.
President Jules Wijdenbosch told the National Assembly the government was "preparing a political response to what is a political action."

Dutch Justice Ministry officials said last week the Netherlands had asked Interpol, the international police organisation, to arrest Bouterse with a view to extraditing him to face drug-trafficking charges.

A defiant Bouterse warned the Netherlands that he was ready for a fight. "If they're looking for trouble, they've come to the right place," Bouterse told members of his ruling National Democratic Party (NDP) late on Monday.
He said he was unconcerned by the arrest warrant and was ready to face his accusers in the Netherlands if guaranteed a safe return to Surinam.
"They're starting something they cannot finish," he said.
Bouterse led coups in 1980 and 1990 and ran a military government in the former Dutch colony for much of the 1980s.
Although he holds no public office, Bouterse was recently made a special adviser to Wijdenbosch and most analysts believe the former military strongman in effect runs the country.
Surinam announced earlier on Tuesday that it was recalling its ambassador from the Hague to discuss its relationship with the former colonial power.
With a population of just over 400,000, Surinam depends heavily on development aid from the Netherlands and has close commercial ties. More than 250,000 Surinamese live there.
But Bouterse said that Surinam was now capable of developing on its own without the Netherlands.
Bouterse has long been distrusted by the Netherlands where he is held responsible by many for ordering the summary execution in 1982 of 15 opposition leaders.
